'''Prince Luiz of Orléans-Braganza''' (6 June 1938 – 15 July 2022) was a Brazilian royal claimant who served as head of the [[House of Orléans-Braganza#Vassouras branch|Vassouras branch]] of the [[Brazilian imperial family|Imperial House of Brazil]] from 1981 until his death. He was the eldest son of [[Pedro Henrique of Orléans-Braganza|Prince Pedro Henrique of Orléans-Braganza]] and [[Princess Maria Elisabeth of Bavaria]], and was regarded by his supporters as [[Pretender to the throne|pretender]] to the defunct title of ''[[Emperor of Brazil]]''.

The Vassouras branch asserts its claim to the former Brazilian throne in opposition to the [[House of Orléans-Braganza#Petrópolis branch|Petrópolis branch]], led by Pedro Carlos Orléans-Braganza. Both Luiz and Pedro Carlos were great-grandsons of [[Isabel, Princess Imperial of Brazil|Princess Isabel]], daughter and heiress of [[Pedro II of Brazil|Emperor Pedro II]], but the two lines diverged following a dynastic dispute involving their fathers, who were first cousins. Throughout his life, Prince Luiz actively upheld the Vassouras claim, engaging in public discourse, monarchist movements, and initiatives related to Brazil’s imperial history and legacy.

== Early life ==
[[File:Filhos de D. Maria Isabel da Baviera e D. Pedro Henrique de Orleans e Bragança.jpg|thumb|Luiz (right) with his mother and siblings, 1957]]
Luiz Gastão Maria José Pio<ref name="Biography">[http://www.monarquia.org.br/domluiz Casa Imperial do Brasil – Biografia de D. Luiz de Orleans e Bragança] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170523164856/http://www.monarquia.org.br/domluiz |date=23 May 2017 }}.</ref> was born on 6 June 1938 in [[Mandelieu-la-Napoule]], [[French Third Republic|France]], as the oldest son of Pedro Henrique of Orléans-Braganza, the Vassouras great-grandson of Emperor [[Pedro II of Brazil]], and his wife, [[Maria Elisabeth of Bavaria]], granddaughter of King [[Ludwig III of Bavaria]].

Prince Luiz was born after the [[revocation]] of the [[exile]] that had been imposed on the Imperial family by Brazil's [[History of Brazil (1889–1930)|first Republican government]]. The aftermath of [[World War I]] and [[World War II]] detained the entire family in Europe until 1945, when the Vassouras branch of the family was finally [[repatriation|repatriated]], settling first in the town of [[Petrópolis]] ([[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]]), then to [[Jacarezinho, Paraná|Jacarezinho]] ([[Paraná (state)|Paraná]]).

In 1957, Prince Luiz returned to Europe to finish his studies, where he graduated in chemistry at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]].<ref>CUNHA, Dionatan da Silveira (2011) (in Portuguese). Príncipe D. Luiz de Orleans e Bragança: 30 Anos de ascensão a Chefia da Casa Imperial do Brasil. ''[http://www.causaimperial.org.br/?p=766 Causa Imperial] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205123635/http://www.causaimperial.org.br/?p=766 |date=5 December 2013 }}''.</ref> Returning to Brazil in 1967, his family having already moved to [[Vassouras]] ([[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]]), Luiz became a member of the [[Tradition, Family and Property|Society for the Defense of Tradition, Family and Property]],<ref>Prince Bertrand of Orleans-Braganza Visits America. ''[http://www.tfp.org/current-campaigns/2001/prince-bertrand-of-orleans-braganza-visits-america.html TFP.org] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120415044301/http://www.tfp.org/current-campaigns/2001/prince-bertrand-of-orleans-braganza-visits-america.html |date=15 April 2012 }}'', 30 April 2001.</ref> a traditionalist [[Roman Catholic|Catholic]] organization which opposes socialistic [[land reform]] and supports conservative politics based on Catholic social doctrine and the principles promoted by [[Plinio Corrêa de Oliveira]]. Alongside [[Duarte Pio, Duke of Braganza]], his Portuguese counterpart and second cousin, he opposed same-sex marital unions, as of a 2015 declaration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://filialsuplicapapa.org/personalities-who-have-signed,3229,c.html|title=Personalidades que firmaron|access-date=1 April 2016|archive-date=23 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170423025802/http://filialsuplicapapa.org/personalities-who-have-signed,3229,c.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Succession ==
On 1981, he succeeded Prince Pedro Henrique as the claimant to the Brazilian throne in the Vassouras branch. According to Brazilian [[legitimist]] claims, he was ''de jure'' Emperor of Brazil ("[[Don (honorific)|Dom]] Luiz I of Brazil").<ref>NÉMETH-TORRES, Geovani (2008) (in Portuguese). A odisséia monarquista no Plebiscito Nacional de 1993. In: ''[https://periodicos.ufba.br/index.php/rvh/article/view/48927 Veredas da História]'', ''1''(1). {{ISSN|1982-4238}}.</ref>

He and two of his younger brothers, Prince [[Bertrand of Orléans-Braganza|Bertrand]] and Prince [[António of Orléans-Braganza|Antônio]], engaged in [[monarchist]] proselytism in Brazil. They played major roles during the campaign for the [[1993 Brazilian constitutional referendum|1993 plebiscite]], which represented the first official opportunity for a return of the monarchy to Brazil since the [[Proclamation of the Republic (Brazil)|Proclamation of the Republic]] in 1889. In it, the people were asked to choose which form of government, [[Presidentialism|presidential]] or [[Parliamentarism|parliamentary]], and which form of state organization, [[republic]] or [[constitutional monarchy]], Brazil should have. The monarchist cause was not successful, receiving 13.2% of the vote against 66% for the republic.<ref>Justiça Eleitoral. [https://www.justicaeleitoral.jus.br/arquivos/plebiscito-de-1993 Resultado Geral do Plebiscito de 1993].</ref>

Dom Luiz resided in a house with "no luxury nor splendor" in [[Higienópolis, São Paulo|Higienópolis]], a borough of [[São Paulo]], Brazil.<ref>SOARES, Regiane (2008) (in Portuguese). Príncipe imperial vive "sem luxo nem esplendor" em casa alugada em SP. ''[https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/folha/brasil/ult96u374584.shtml Folha Online]'', 4 March 2008.</ref>

==Death==

Prince Luiz died in São Paulo on 14 July 2022 following a month-long hospitalization.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/politica/2022/07/5022626-morre-dom-luiz-de-orleans-e-braganca-bisneto-da-princesa-isabel.html | title=Morre dom Luiz de Orleans e Bragança, bisneto da Princesa Isabel }}</ref> The following day, Brazilian President [[Jair Bolsonaro]], countersigned by the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Brazil)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]], issued a decree declaring a [[national day of mourning]] in his honor.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2019-2022/2022/decreto/D11134.htm | title=DECRETO Nº 11.134, DE 15 DE JULHO DE 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://noticias.uol.com.br/politica/ultimas-noticias/2022/07/15/dom-luiz-de-orleans-e-braganca-luto-bolsonaro.htm | title=Bolsonaro decreta luto oficial pela morte de Dom Luiz de Orleans e Bragança }}</ref>

As Head of the House of Orléans-Braganza, Prine Luiz Gastão held the following positions:<ref name="Anuário">Pró-Monarquia. (2022). [https://monarquia.org.br/a-familia-imperial/anuario-da-casa-imperial Anuário da Casa Imperial do Brasil]. São Paulo: Pró-Monarquia, 25.</ref>
* [[File:Imperial Order of Christ (Brasil).gif|50px]] Grand Master and Sovereign of the [[Order of Christ (Brazil)|Imperial Order of Christ]]
* [[File:Imperial Order of Saint Benedict of Aviz (Brazil) - ribbon bar.png|50px]] Grand Master and Sovereign of the [[Order of Aviz (Brazil)|Imperial Order of Saint Benedict of Aviz]]
* [[File:PRT Order of Saint James of the Sword - Knight BAR.svg|50px]] Grand Master and Sovereign of the [[Imperial Order of Saint James of the Sword]]
* [[File:BRA - Order of the Southern Cross - Knight BAR.svg|50px]] Grand Master and Sovereign of the [[Order of the Southern Cross|Imperial Order of the Southern Cross]]
* [[File:Imperial Order of Pedro I.gif|50px]] Grand Master and Sovereign of the [[Order of Pedro I|Imperial Order of Emperor Pedro I]]
* [[File:BRA Ordem de Rosa Gra Cruz Efetiva.png|50px]] Grand Master and Sovereign of the [[Order of the Rose|Imperial Order of the Rose]]

Prince Luiz has also been decorated with a number of other honours:<ref name="Anuário" />
* [[File:ESP Sacred Military Constantinian Order of Saint George Justicia BAR.svg|50px]] Bailiff Grand Cross of the [[Sacred Military Constantinian Order of Saint George]]
* [[File:PRT Ordem de Nossa Senhora da Conceicao de Vila Vicosa Cavaleiro ribbon.svg|50px]]  Grand Cross of the [[Order of the Immaculate Conception of Vila Viçosa]]
* [[File:SMOM-gcs.svg|50px]] Bailiff Grand Cross of Honour and Devotion of the [[Sovereign Military Order of Malta]]
* [[File:OESSG Cavaliere BAR.jpg|50px]] Knight of the [[Order of the Holy Sepulchre (Catholic)|Order of the Holy Sepulchre]]<ref>MARIE, Michelle (2012) (in Portuguese).
